title: Mirabel and the Protocol
premise: Bram Iversen, a veteran navigator who has spent two decades ferrying cargo past the sleeping backup clones stored in his own hold, is conscripted when the Meridian returns from deep space carrying its entire crew de-aged to their twenties — living proof that the 'Protocol,' a treaty technology both fleets believe only they possess, actually works. The Protocol is a lie Bram's dead wife helped build: a fake immortality program designed to keep the Concord and the Verge fleets from open war, sustained by staged miracles like the Meridian. When the de-aged crew begins remembering their true lives and a Verge defector exposes the fraud, Bram must choose between preserving the peace built on his wife's deception and telling a truth that will ignite the fleets. In the end, he broadcasts the whole lie along with her final message — reframing the Protocol not as immortality but as a shared choice to stop fighting — buying a fragile, honest truce at the cost of his ship, his secret cargo of backups, and nearly his life.
about_author: Jonah Blackwood is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. Their work explores the moral weight carried by people who keep systems running that no one else wants to look at.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Bram Iversen runs a routine cargo jump through contested Verge space, avoiding a Concord patrol while thinking about the forty backup clones in cold storage beneath his feet — cargo he's never been paid enough to question. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: weary complicity; a man who has stopped asking what he carries.

chapters.title: Signal from the Long Dark
chapters.summary: A distress ping from the Meridian, missing for thirty years, drags Bram off-course. Docking at relay station Kestrel, he watches the ancient ship arrive crewed by people young enough to be the original sailors' grandchildren. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: uncanny dread sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Aboard the Meridian, Bram meets Captain Sefa Oyelaran, biologically twenty-six but with thirty years of memories, and her crew, all restored to youth by an event they can't explain. Concord officials seal the ship within hours. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief — she remembers dying.

chapters.title: The Man from Oversight
chapters.summary: Concord envoy Darius Venn commandeers Bram's ship to transport sealed evidence from the Meridian, threatening to impound the Kestrel if he refuses. Venn knows too much about Bram's hold. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: trapped; the past closing in.

chapters.title: What Ilse Built
chapters.summary: Sorting the sealed crates, Bram finds his late wife Ilse's handwriting on Protocol schematics — documents dated after her death. Flashbacks reveal she was a Protocol architect who faked her death to disappear into the project. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with longing.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Miracle
chapters.summary: At the Concord capital, Bram learns the truth: the Protocol is a fabricated immortality program, and the Meridian's 'miracle' was staged to terrify both fleets into truce. The de-aged crew are unwitting actors. POV: Venn. Emotional beat: cold clarity; power as stagecraft.

chapters.title: Sefa Remembers Dying
chapters.summary: Sefa's recovered memories fracture the cover story — she recalls the real accident, the real deaths, and being copied. She confronts Venn privately and is warned into silence. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: horror curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest, Forty Names
chapters.summary: Bram decrypts his own hold and discovers his backups aren't merchandise — they're spares for the Protocol's next staged miracle, and one of them is Ilse. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: devastation; love weaponized against him.

chapters.title: The Verge Sends an Audience
chapters.summary: Verge observers arrive to inspect the miracle, led by the sharp-eyed Auditor Rhys Tanaka, who notices the Meridian's logs were rewritten in Concord cipher. Bram is ordered to charm him into ignorance. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: performance under pressure; unexpected kinship with the enemy.

chapters.title: A Lie Held by Two Hands
chapters.summary: Tanaka and Bram, drinking in a dockside bar, trade half-truths until each realizes the other already suspects everything. Neither can say it aloud. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: lonely intimacy; two men guarding the same secret for opposite sides.

chapters.title: Ilse, Awake
chapters.summary: Technicians begin activating the backups for the next staging. Bram secretly wakes the Ilse copy early in a maintenance bay — she has her memories up to her 'death' and doesn't know she's a copy. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: tender, terrible reunion built on a fresh deception.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: A Meridian crew member defects to the Verge with partial proof the miracle was staged. Both fleets mobilize; the truce clock starts ticking. Venn orders Bram to hunt the defector using his smuggler's routes. POV: Venn. Emotional beat: desperation dressed as command.

chapters.title: Hunting a Ghost
chapters.summary: Bram tracks the defector through asteroid refuges but lets her slip away, tipping Tanaka off instead. He chooses the fragile alliance over his orders. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet treason; relief and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: What Copies Owe
chapters.summary: Ilse discovers the backup bay and understands what she is. Instead of collapsing, she demands to help finish what she started — on her terms. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade as agency.

chapters.title: Venn's Gambit
chapters.summary: With the defector loose, Venn plans a bigger, crueler miracle: publicly 'resurrecting' Ilse to reset the narrative, whatever it costs Bram. Bram realizes Venn knew about the hold all along. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: rage; the puppeteer unmasked too late.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Miracle
chapters.summary: Bram, Ilse, Sefa, and Tanaka meet in secret aboard the Kestrel and decide to seize the broadcast themselves — to tell the truth before Venn can stage another lie. Each has something to lose. POV: rotating brief sections. Emotional beat: conspiratorial hope, fragile as glass.

chapters.title: Staging Ground
chapters.summary: The fleets converge on the Meridian for the resurrection ceremony. Bram smuggles his team aboard among the technical crews while Venn's security closes around them. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension; homecoming turned battlefield.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mid-ceremony, Ilse takes the stage as herself and hijacks the fleet-wide feed, exposing the Protocol — then plays her own final message: the lie was never immortality, it was a pause, and the pause belongs to everyone now. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as inheritance.

chapters.title: Fleets at the Trigger
chapters.summary: Both fleets hover on the edge of war as hardliners move to silence the broadcast. Venn orders the Kestrel destroyed with Bram aboard; Tanaka refuses the order and turns the Verge guns aside. POV: Tanaka. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience.

chapters.title: Burning the Hold
chapters.summary: To prove no one controls resurrection, Bram vents and burns his own backup cargo — including every remaining copy of Ilse — live on the feed. The gesture disarms both fleets more than any weapon could. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrificial grief; freedom through loss.

chapters.title: Truce of Honest Men
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Sefa mediates a raw accord: joint oversight of the real science, amnesty for the Meridian crew, Venn arrested by his own oversight board. The lie dies so something true can grow. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned peace.

chapters.title: One Navigator, One Ship
chapters.summary: Months later, Bram flies the scarred Kestrel on ordinary runs again, Ilse's final message tucked in his nav archive. Sefa sends word the first joint research vessel launches soon — and asks if he'll navigate. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; carrying the past forward without being owned by it.
